programs.description: An eight-part docuseries exploring Earth's major eras and extinction events across 450 million years alongside the creatures who fought to survive.

Hitting the gas with hawks, cheetahs, and other speed demons to learn why first-in-class acceleration can be an evolutionary advantage, then pumping the brakes with Earth's biggest slowpokes to see why, sometimes, slow and steady wins the race.

Mountains, rocks and steep cliffs, no place for a predator relying on their speed. But that's exactly where we find our two magnificent Cheetah mothers. Hidden between the mountains, open savannah plains miraculously appear. And on these savannahs.
A mother rhinoceros trains her two-year-old son to survive in the grasslands of Uganda, and both undergo a test of time when she gives birth to a new calf.
Mediterranean Hunters
The intimate lives of lions, leopards and cheetahs of the Masai Mara; a journey of motherhood, survival, and territorial battles.

Explores some of the most dangerous predators in the wild and calculates how risk it is for a human to protect themselves against them.
Tigers in general are believed to be solitary hunters. But in the forests of Central India, a gang of females learned to hunt co-operatively, taking down large, dangerous prey.

The seasonal changes of the Luangwa Valley are extraordinarily intense. Heavy rains transform the Luangwa River from a shallow channel into a majestic waterway where grass grows tall and streams fill with an abundant selection of creatures.

Across the planet, wolves and lions lead two legendary predator lineages: canids and felines. We explore their differences and similarities, from brute strength to social intelligence, revealing who dominates in each territory.
Zimbabwe is the perfect habitat for Africa's finest predator. Follow the development of four cubs, from two weeks to three years old, as they progress from 'Cute to Killer'.

The life story of a charismatic hippo in Zambia's Luangwa Valley. Over 35 years, he grows from a small calf to a full-fledged leader. His experiences make him stronger and stronger, until he is ready for kingship.
Filmed over ten years, an in-depth look at the leopard characters of South Africa and their fascinating unfolding story once their Queen dies.

Located just 10 miles from New York's Times Square, the Bronx Zoo is a recognised world leader in animal care and species conservation. It houses more than 6,000 animals and has a staff of 500-plus people dedicated to their care and well-being. Never before have camera crews been granted full access to the 265-acre campus, until production of the docuseries `The Zoo'. The results are stories focusing on dozens of animals and experiences at the facility, and its critical mission to conserve wildlife around the world. Episodes also highlight various employees and how their expertise and skills help provide top-quality care for the animals.

Carrying on late wildlife conservationist Steve Irwin's mission to bring people closer to animals is now the mission of his family. Terri, Bindi and Robert Irwin return to Animal Planet, giving viewers access to their wildlife adventures around the world and the amazing animals that continue to inspire their conservation efforts. The series features the family caring for more than 1,200 animals at the Australia Zoo; overseeing a world-class wildlife hospital, the largest of its kind in the world; and conducting high-level global expeditions.
Explores stunning natural landscapes and how animals act on their protective and fierce nature to survive and reproduce.

Our protagonist, the actor and naturalist Arturo Islas travels through the going into their jungles, deserts, and seas in search of the wonderful species of fauna: mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish, and insects. WILD BY NATURE is a great experience of adventure and knowledge of natural wealth.

From the makers of Earth's Greatest Rivers, Earth's Tropical Islands journeys to three of the most exotic, mysterious and remote islands on planet Earth: Madagascar, Borneo and Hawaii. In three episodes, the series reveals how these isolated and iconic tropical islands harbour remarkable wildlife and human castaways found nowhere else on Earth. Madagascar is the oldest island in the world, Borneo cradles more diversity of life than any other island, and Hawaii is the remotest island chain in the world. In a rapidly changing world, these fragile islands are a vital gauge for the health of our planet.

It houses more than 6,000 animals and has a staff of 500-plus people dedicated to their care and well-being. Never before have camera crews been granted full access to the 265-acre campus, until production of the docuseries `The Zoo'. The results are stories focusing on dozens of animals and experiences at the facility, and its critical mission to conserve wildlife around the world. Episodes also highlight various employees and how their expertise and skills help provide top-quality care for the animals.
